questions.q: A customer insists they already paid an invoice that still shows open. What should be checked first?
options: Immediately write off the balance to resolve the dispute
Whether a receipt exists for that customer sitting unapplied, on-account, or stuck in a lockbox exceptions queue
Whether the customer's credit limit needs to be increased
Whether the customer should be merged with another account
questions.explain: Before assuming anything is actually missing, check for unapplied or on-account cash, or a lockbox batch that failed validation — this is one of the most common false alarms in receivables.

questions.q: During period close, GL's Accounts Receivable balance is higher than what Receivables shows. Besides an unaccounted transaction, what else should be checked?
options: Whether a dunning letter was sent that month
Whether a customer statement was generated
Whether the receipt method allows automatic creation
Whether a manual journal entry was made directly in GL, bypassing Receivables
questions.explain: A manual journal entry made directly in the General Ledger, bypassing the Receivables subledger, is a classic cause of GL being overstated relative to Receivables.

questions.q: A customer disputes part of an invoice as a billing error but doesn't dispute the rest. How should the disputed portion be resolved?
options: With a transaction write-off, since the customer disagrees with it
By ignoring it until the next period close
By merging the customer with a different account
With an adjustment, since the underlying number is actually wrong
questions.explain: A genuine billing error means the number itself is incorrect, which calls for an adjustment — not a write-off, which is for balances that are correct but uncollectible.

questions.q: What should happen to the undisputed portion of a long-overdue balance before it is considered for write-off?
options: It should be written off immediately since it is old
It should go through collections and dunning, with write-off only considered after those efforts are genuinely exhausted
It should be converted into a miscellaneous receipt
It should be merged into the disputed portion
questions.explain: A write-off is a last resort after collections efforts have failed — age alone does not justify skipping straight to a write-off.

questions.q: What course comes next in the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path after Oracle Fusion Accounts Receivable?
options: Oracle Fusion Procure-to-Pay
SQL for Oracle Financials
Oracle Fusion Security
Oracle Fusion Cash Management
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion Cash Management is the first course in the Financial Operations stage, which follows directly after the Financials Configuration stage that includes Accounts Receivable.
